_about: Per connector kind: whether the database can call a model on its own (store_side_models: true / false / 'unknown'), and the exact setting to change for each kind of model-egress finding. 'false' marks a product fact (capability_limit); 'unknown' is never read as 'no egress'. Remediation text names vendor settings verified against the cited documentation.

weaviate.features: Vectorizer (text2vec-*), reranker and generative modules call model providers from the server. All API-based modules are available by default from Weaviate v1.33.

remediation.third_party: Set the collection's vectorizer to none (Configure.Vectors.self_provided) and embed client-side, or switch to a self-hosted text2vec-transformers (or text2vec-ollama) module so text never leaves your network.
remediation.configured_unused: Limit ENABLE_MODULES to the modules you use; from v1.33 API-based modules are enabled by default, so list the ones you need explicitly.
remediation.api_key_auth: Pass provider keys per request as headers from the client rather than storing them in the server environment, and rotate any key that was stored.

azure_search.features: Index vectorizers and indexer skills call Azure OpenAI or Foundry model endpoints at query and index time.

remediation.third_party: Point the vectorizer's resourceUri at an Azure OpenAI or Foundry resource in your own tenant and region, or remove the vectorizer and send query vectors from the client.
remediation.api_key_auth: Remove apiKey from azureOpenAIParameters and leave authIdentity empty (system-assigned managed identity) or set it to a user-assigned identity with the Cognitive Services OpenAI User role.
remediation.configured_unused: Delete vectorizers that no vector field's profile references.

opensearch.features: ML Commons remote-model connectors call external model endpoints from the cluster (neural search, ingest processors).

remediation.third_party: Deploy the model locally in ML Commons, or point the connector at a model endpoint in your own cloud account, and remove connectors to third-party APIs.
remediation.trusted_endpoints: Replace broad entries in plugins.ml_commons.trusted_connector_endpoints_regex with anchored HTTPS patterns for each approved host (for example ^https://bedrock-runtime\..*[a-z0-9-]\.amazonaws\.com/.*$), and enable plugins.ml_commons.connector_access_control_enabled.
remediation.api_key_auth: Prefer IAM-role credentials for AWS connectors over API keys held in connector credentials, and rotate stored keys.
remediation.configured_unused: Delete connectors that no deployed model uses.

milvus.features: Embedding functions (Milvus 2.6+) call OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, DashScope, Bedrock, Vertex AI, Voyage AI, Cohere, SiliconFlow, Hugging Face and others at insert and search; credentials live in milvus.yaml.

remediation.third_party: Drop the collection's TEXTEMBEDDING function and insert client-computed vectors, or use a self-hosted Hugging Face TEI endpoint.
remediation.api_key_auth: Move provider keys out of the milvus.yaml credential section into your secret manager, and rotate keys that were stored there.

qdrant.features: Qdrant Cloud Inference embeds with Qdrant-hosted models, or proxies to OpenAI, Cohere, Jina AI and OpenRouter with the caller's key. Enabled by default for clusters created after 7 July 2025.

remediation.third_party: Upsert and query with client-computed vectors instead of documents that name an external-provider model, or use a Qdrant-hosted model so no further provider receives the text.

pinecone.features: Integrated inference embeds and reranks with models hosted on Pinecone's own infrastructure.

remediation.third_party: Create the index without an integrated embedding model and upsert client-computed vectors.

mongodb.features: Vector Search Automated Embedding (autoEmbed index fields) calls Voyage AI models at index and query time.

remediation.third_party: Replace the autoEmbed field in the Vector Search index with a vector field and store client-computed embeddings.
remediation.api_key_auth: Prefer Atlas-managed Voyage AI keys over keys configured on self-managed mongot, and use separate keys for indexing and query as MongoDB recommends.

pgvector.features: Extensions such as azure_ai (Azure Database for PostgreSQL) and Google Cloud SQL model endpoint management call model endpoints from SQL.

remediation.third_party: Compute embeddings in the application, or point the extension at a model endpoint in your own tenant.
remediation.api_key_auth: Do not store provider keys with azure_ai.set_setting('azure_openai.subscription_key', ...); use a managed identity where the service supports it, and rotate stored keys.

vertex_ai.features: Vector Search 2.0 collections can autogenerate embeddings with a Vertex AI model (vertex_embedding_config). Vector Search 1.0 indexes take precomputed vectors only.

remediation.third_party: Vertex AI models run in your own project; no third party receives the text.

bedrock_kb.features: The knowledge base's embedding model (and any parsing or generation model) is a Bedrock model in your account.

remediation.third_party: Bedrock models run in your AWS account; check the data retention mode and any cross-region inference profile instead.

openai.features: OpenAI embeds files attached to a vector store; the store and the model are the same operator.

remediation.third_party: The data is already held by OpenAI; record OpenAI as a sub-processor with its DPA.

redis.not_supported_reason: Redis stores and searches vectors it is given; embedding happens in the client (for example RedisVL), so the server sends no text to a model provider.

chroma.features: Embedding functions normally run in the client library. Whether Chroma Cloud embeds server-side for this deployment is not reported to this connector.
